next_steps: Sophie to send updated cost model with dedicated vs hosted scenarios by 2028-07-21
Marco to run a short 24-hour latency/cost benchmark with Aurelia's sample traffic (token mix attached) by 2028-07-25
Maya and Redwood security team to schedule SOC2 scoping call for private deployment on 2028-07-26
Priya and Tom to share SLOs and traffic spikes calendar for Q3 by 2028-07-20
action_items: Owner: Marco Chen; Item: Run 24h perf/cost benchmark using Llama-70B-4bit baseline + prefix caching; Due: 2028-07-25
Owner: Sophie Patel; Item: Share updated pricing scenarios and drafting pilot statement of work; Due: 2028-07-21
Owner: Maya Singh; Item: Provide Aurelia minimal compliance pack & list of required evidence for SOC2 scoping; Due: 2028-07-22

meeting_header: Date: 2028-07-18 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Daniel Kim (Aurelia Head of ML), Priya Rao (Eng Manager), Oliver Barnes (Finance), Maya Singh (Security), Tom Erickson (SRE)
summary: Quarterly health sprint to align on runway for inference usage, cost scenarios (hosted vs dedicated vs private), immediate reliability mitigations for Q3 spikes, and security scoping for private deployment. Agreed pilot metrics and next steps for benchmarks and pricing design.
topics: dedicated vs hosted vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
00:00 Sophie: alright everyone thanks for joining, um, we've got about an hour, goal is to align on runway and next steps for the pilot. quick roll call.
00:12 Daniel: hey Sophie, Daniel here. thanks.
00:15 Priya: Priya on my side.
00:17 Oliver: Oliver, finance.
00:19 Maya: Maya, security.
00:21 Tom: Tom here, SRE.
00:23 Sophie: great. Marco from our infra team will lead the perf bits. Marco?
00:28 Marco: hey all, yeah quick agenda: usage snapshot, cost scenarios, a quick dive into latency incidents last month, and then security/deploy options.
00:39 Daniel: sounds good. i guess starting with usage — we've been seeing that the summaries pipeline spiked in June, about 35% above forecast, tokens per request went up because of longer contexts.
00:52 Lena: we pulled the token burn in the console, and yes june spike correlates with the new recommendation rollout on mobile which increased sequence length.
01:04 Priya: the mobile rollout was intentional but we expected caching to help, it looks like prefix cache didn't kick in on some routes because of slight prompt variation.
01:16 Marco: yeah that's a classic prefix mismatch; we saw a 20% loss in effective KV cache hit rate on those routes. we can show autotune recommendations — changing the batching window and enabling fuzzy prefix mapping reduces cost.
01:29 Daniel: can you quantify impact? we need runway for the next 3 months.
01:33 Marco: ballpark — with current hosted setup, the spike increased monthly token spend by ~42k USD. with caching tweaks + 4-bit quantized variants we'd expect to reduce that by 30-45% depending on tail latency tolerances.
01:50 Oliver: 42k was one month? that's material. what about dedicated reserved capacity — how different is the unit economics?
02:00 Sophie: good question. dedicated can be 30-60% cheaper per effective token at steady state but has commit and utilization risk. we prepared a base vs dedicated vs private cost sheet, i'll share.
02:12 Oliver: please do, finance will need the assumptions. are GPU costs included for the private on-prem option?
02:18 Sophie: yes, the private option model includes hardware+ops overhead; key thing is we assume Aurelia would run their own KMS or HSM for private, which affects cost and compliance.
02:30 Maya: on the compliance note — SOC2 is a must for us. we also need audit logs with token-level redaction and evidence for key lifecycle management. can Redwood support that out of the box?
02:42 Marco: short answer — yes. we have audit logs, KMS integrations (cloud KMS + HSM options), and the private control plane supports customer-managed keys. we'll need a scoping call to map evidence.
02:54 Maya: okay, scoping call would help. also data residency: some customer PII is processed and must stay in eu-west1 for those users. can routing guarantee region pinning?
03:07 Sophie: yes, region pinning is supported in both hosted and dedicated policies; private obviously gives you full control.
03:13 Tom: our main concern is tail latency during traffic bursts. we saw 600ms 95p on generate endpoints which caused client timeouts. any suggestions?
03:23 Marco: two levers: fast-path model variants (quantized + distillation) and autoscale headroom. also prefix caching for warm contexts reduces p95 significantly. we can set a safety pool of reserved GPUs for burst handling.
03:38 Daniel: what's the latency hit for 4-bit quantized vs fp16?
03:43 Marco: typically 4-bit gives slight accuracy degradation on edge cases; latency improves by ~25-40% and cost drops significantly. for many of your summarization tasks the quality delta is negligible. we should validate on your prompt set.
03:56 Daniel: that's acceptable if we don't regress business metrics. can we A/B?
04:00 Sophie: yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and A/B; we can route a small percentage to the quantized variant and watch metrics.
04:07 Priya: timeline — we'd like a pilot ready in late august to coincide with our Q4 readiness window. is that feasible?
04:15 Sophie: feasible. immediate plan: benchmark, pilot SOW, security scoping. Marco — how long for the benchmark?
04:23 Marco: if Aurelia provides anonymized traces and token distribution, we can run a 24-72 hour benchmark within a week. need the traces and a sample load generator.
04:33 Tom: we'll anonymize and pull the traces by friday. any special format?
04:37 Marco: CSV token distribution + gzipped request samples works fine. we'll share a template.
04:42 Sophia: (note: transcription shows Sophie as Sophia here — occasional mislabel)
04:44 Maya: on encryption, do you support customer-managed keys for hosted API or only for private?
04:49 Marco: hosted can integrate with customer CMEK in selected cloud providers but full HSM-backed key control is best in private. we can document what level of key separation we provide for hosted.
04:58 Oliver: license and billing — if we move to dedicated mid-pilot, how do we handle commit credits and overage?
05:05 Sophie: typically we propose a reserved capacity with burstable pools; pilot starts on hosted usage billing and the committed contract is negotiated once we hit steady utilization thresholds. credits can be applied pro-rata. we'll include options in the pricing doc.
05:18 Daniel: a couple of technical deep dive items we want: (1) exact attack surface for prompt leakage, (2) redaction guarantees on logs, (3) runbook for model rollback on drift. can Redwood meet those?
05:32 Marco: yes to all. we have a model rollback system with automated fallback to previous model versions, and redaction can be applied at ingestion before logs hit storage. we'll share the runbook excerpt.
05:43 Maya: perfect. for SOC2 evidence we need the controls mapped to our auditor template. can the Redwood security team map controls?
05:51 Sophie: yes, we'll align security teams and do a controls mapping session next week.
05:57 Lena: quick CSM note — we noticed a steady 2% error increase on the reranker endpoint after the June rollout; not customer-facing yet but worth tracking in the pilot.
06:08 Daniel: ok we'll put that on the pilot acceptance criteria.
06:12 Priya: on instrumentation, we need token-level cost attribution per route and by API key for internal chargeback. is that already available?
06:21 Marco: yes, console supports token attribution per API key and per route. we can also stream metrics to your internal observability via webhook or prometheus push.
06:31 Oliver: do you leak model names in responses? compliance wants model provenance tracked but not necessarily exposed to end users.
06:38 Marco: we can annotate logs with model provenance and strip it from user-facing responses.
06:43 Tom: a question about burst protection — can Redwood throttle at the per-customer level before hitting our downstream backends?
06:52 Marco: Redwood supports rate limits and per-API-key throttles and can send back a structured 429 with retry-after. we can also set graceful degradation policies that fall back to smaller models during overload.
07:05 Daniel: excellent. can we see a concrete cost example for our current 200M tokens/month baseline, with a 25% growth scenario?
07:15 Sophie: yes, i'll include three scenarios in the updated cost sheet: hosted (baseline), hosted+optimizations, and dedicated commitments at 6/12 months.
07:25 Oliver: include assumptions on cache hit % and avg tokens per call please.
07:29 Sophie: noted.
07:31 Priya: regarding model versions — if we pin a version for pilot, how are security patches handled?
07:37 Marco: you can pin model artifact versions; security patches to the runtime are rolled through channels. critical security patches can be expedited; we document patch windows in the SOW.
07:47 Daniel: last month we saw a cross-region failover issue; how does Redwood handle cross-region routing?
07:53 Marco: smart routing policy routes by region, and fallback policies route to a compatible model variant in a secondary region. we can set RTO targets in the SLA.
08:05 Maya: SLA — can we get 99.9 for p95 and a separate uptime SLO for control plane?
08:12 Sophie: yes, enterprise SLAs can be scoped. control plane uptime is typically higher; we'll map specifics in the contract.
08:20 Lena: quick adoption note — recommend a runbook for developers on prompt normalization to improve caching. simple changes lowered token burn for another customer by ~18%.
08:33 Priya: we'll socialize that to our client teams.
08:36 Daniel: any blockers you see for running the pilot?
08:39 Marco: technical blockers are minimal; main things are sample traces, security evidence, and finalizing pilot metrics.
08:47 Oliver: finance needs clarity on the commitment trigger threshold. can you propose a utilization threshold?
08:53 Sophie: yes, we'll propose a util threshold and a 90-day review clause.
08:58 Tom: one more SRE ask — can we have a synthetic harness that matches our spike pattern to validate autoscale behavior?
09:05 Marco: yes, we'll provide a harness template and help run an initial soak test.
09:11 Daniel: brilliant.
09:13 Sophie: ok let's recap — Marco runs the benchmark once you share traces; Sophie will send cost scenarios and SOW draft; Maya and our security team will schedule SOC2 scoping; Tom provides traces and spike calendar. any other open items?
09:30 Maya: please cc our security alias on the artifact share.
09:35 Sophie: will do.
09:36 Priya: put the pilot acceptance criteria in a shared doc so engineering and product can sign off.
09:42 Sophie: yes we'll draft acceptance criteria and circulate.
09:45 Daniel: timeline check — if benchmarks complete by 25th and SOW agreed by 21st, pilot kickoff late August aligns.
09:55 Sophie: sounds good. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and Slack.
10:00 (meeting ends)

Notes: shared deck link: https://redwood.ai/decks/aurelia-qbr 
Benchmarks: Marco to use Llama-70B-4bit baseline + quantized variants; sample trace template: https://redwood.ai/samples/trace-template.csv
